bloff.q: What is Scotland's national animal?
bloff.fakta: The unicorn has been a Scottish symbol since the 1400s – in the royal coat of arms it is shown in chains.

bloff.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
bloff.fakta: Two of the hearts pump blood through the gills, the third sends it round the rest of the body.

bloff.q: What was Coca-Cola originally sold as?
bloff.fakta: The pharmacist John Pemberton made it in 1886 and sold it as a tonic for things like headaches.

bloff.q: What is a group of flamingos called?
bloff.fakta: Flamingos are pink because they eat algae and tiny crustaceans full of pigment.

bloff.q: Which country has the most lakes in the world?
bloff.fakta: Around 60 per cent of all the world's lakes are in Canada.

bloff.q: What was Google called before it was called Google?
bloff.fakta: The search engine was called BackRub because it counted the links pointing back to web pages.

bloff.q: How long did the shortest war in history last?
bloff.fakta: The war between Britain and Zanzibar in 1896 was over after about 38 minutes.

bloff.q: What colour is a polar bear's skin?
bloff.fakta: The fur is actually see-through – it looks white because it scatters the light.

bloff.q: What is the fear of long words called?
bloff.fakta: The word was made as long as possible on purpose – a joke at the expense of those who fear it.

bloff.q: Which country invented the cheese slicer?
bloff.fakta: Thor Bjørklund from Lillehammer patented the cheese slicer in 1925.

bloff.q: During World War II, what did Norwegians wear paper clips as a symbol of?
bloff.fakta: Norwegians wore paper clips on their lapels as a quiet sign of unity against the occupiers.

bloff.q: Which animal has cube-shaped poop?
bloff.fakta: Wombats leave the little cubes on rocks and logs to mark their territory.

bloff.q: What is the plastic tip at the end of a shoelace called?
bloff.fakta: The word comes from the French aiguillette, “little needle”.

bloff.q: What animal is on the flag of Wales?
bloff.fakta: The red dragon, Y Ddraig Goch, has been a Welsh symbol for more than a thousand years.

bloff.q: Which bird can fly backwards?
bloff.fakta: Hummingbirds can also hover in place – their wings beat in a figure of eight.

bloff.q: Which planet spins the opposite way to most of the others?
bloff.fakta: On Venus the sun rises in the west, and a day there is longer than a year.

bloff.q: How many eyes does a honeybee have?
bloff.fakta: A bee has two large compound eyes and three small simple eyes on top of its head.

bloff.q: What is the world's most expensive spice?
bloff.fakta: Each crocus flower gives just three tiny stigmas – it takes around 150,000 flowers for one kilo.

bloff.q: How many legs does a lobster have?
bloff.fakta: The lobster is a ten-legged crustacean – the two biggest legs are the claws.

bloff.q: Which US state has only one syllable in its name?
bloff.fakta: Maine is also the only state that borders just one other state.

bloff.q: Where does the Tetris theme come from?
bloff.fakta: The tune is the 19th-century folk song “Korobeiniki”, about a travelling pedlar.

bloff.q: Which riding animal can’t throw up?
bloff.fakta: The muscles at the entrance to the stomach are so strong that food only goes one way.

bloff.q: Where in the body is the smallest bone?
bloff.fakta: The stirrup bone in the middle ear is only about three millimetres long.

bloff.q: What does the name LEGO mean?
bloff.fakta: Ole Kirk Christiansen made up the name from “leg godt” in 1934.

bloff.q: Which country has the most pyramids?
bloff.fakta: Sudan has more than 200 pyramids from the ancient kingdom of Kush – more than Egypt.

bloff.q: What colour were carrots before they were orange?
bloff.fakta: Orange carrots became common in the Netherlands in the 1600s.

bloff.q: Which animal has the strongest bite in the world?
bloff.fakta: Its bite has been measured at more than 16,000 newtons – more than any other animal tested.

bloff.q: What is Norway's national instrument?
bloff.fakta: The Hardanger fiddle has four or five extra strings underneath that ring along as you play.

bloff.q: Which city was Norway's capital before Oslo?
bloff.fakta: Bergen was the capital in the 1200s, before King Haakon V moved power to Oslo around 1300.

bloff.q: Which mammal with a bill lays eggs?
bloff.fakta: The platypus has no stomach either – its gullet goes straight to the gut.

bloff.q: Which country has the most time zones (counting all its territories)?
bloff.fakta: With all its overseas territories, France spans 12 time zones.

bloff.q: What was the name of the first cloned sheep?
bloff.fakta: Dolly was born in Scotland in 1996 and named after Dolly Parton.

bloff.q: Which fruit is actually a berry: the banana or the strawberry?
bloff.fakta: Botanically, a strawberry is not a berry – its seeds are on the outside.

bloff.q: What colour is an octopus’s blood?
bloff.fakta: The blood uses copper instead of iron to carry oxygen, which makes it blue.

bloff.q: What is the largest ocean in the world?
bloff.fakta: The Pacific is bigger than all the land on Earth put together.

bloff.q: Which letter doesn't appear in the name of any US state?
bloff.fakta: By comparison, J appears in just one state name: New Jersey.

bloff.q: Which city gets a Christmas tree from Oslo every year as thanks for its help during WWII?
bloff.fakta: The tree comes from the forests around Oslo and has stood in Trafalgar Square every year since 1947.

bloff.q: How many keys does a standard piano have?
bloff.fakta: 52 white and 36 black.

bloff.q: Which is the only continent without ants?
bloff.fakta: Ants live on every other continent, and more than 12,000 species are known.

bloff.q: Which teeth do giraffes not have in their upper jaw?
bloff.fakta: Giraffes strip leaves with their tongue against a hard dental pad in the upper jaw.

bloff.q: Which country has the most islands in the world?
bloff.fakta: Sweden has more than 260,000 islands, and most of them are uninhabited.

bloff.q: How many times wider than Earth is the sun?
bloff.fakta: More than a million Earths would fit inside the sun.

bloff.q: What was the first product ever scanned with a barcode in a shop?
bloff.fakta: It was a pack of Wrigley's gum in a shop in Ohio in 1974.

bloff.q: Which animal sleeps with half its brain at a time?
bloff.fakta: One half of the brain rests while the other keeps it breathing and watching for danger.

bloff.q: What colour is a flamingo when it hatches?
bloff.fakta: The pink colour only arrives after a couple of years, from its food.

bloff.q: Which country drinks the most coffee per person?
bloff.fakta: The average Finn drinks around 12 kilos of coffee a year.

bloff.q: How much water can a thirsty camel drink in one go?
bloff.fakta: The water isn't stored in the hump – it's full of fat.

bloff.q: What is a group of crows called in English?
bloff.fakta: The name comes from old folklore that crows foretold death.

bloff.q: What is the longest fjord in Norway?
bloff.fakta: The Sognefjord is more than 200 kilometres long and over 1,300 metres deep.

bloff.q: What is the name of Snoopy’s brother?
bloff.fakta: Spike lives alone in the desert outside Needles, California.

bloff.q: Which country has the oldest national flag still in use?
bloff.fakta: According to legend, the Dannebrog fell from the sky in 1219.

bloff.q: What is the name of Pippi Longstocking’s horse?
bloff.fakta: Pippi is so strong she can lift the horse with her bare hands.

bloff.q: What was bubble wrap originally meant to be?
bloff.fakta: Two inventors made it in 1957 as textured wallpaper – it only took off as packaging.

bloff.q: What was Play-Doh originally sold as?
bloff.fakta: When people stopped heating with coal, nobody needed the wallpaper cleaner any more – so it became a toy.

bloff.q: Which country produces the most coffee in the world?
bloff.fakta: Brazil has been the world's biggest coffee producer for more than 150 years.

bloff.q: What is the world’s highest waterfall?
bloff.fakta: The water drops 979 metres – almost a kilometre.

bloff.q: Which planet has the most known moons?
bloff.fakta: Saturn has more than 270 known moons, and more keep being found.

bloff.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
bloff.fakta: More precisely, about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.

bloff.q: Which internal organ can grow back?
bloff.fakta: Even with only a quarter left, the liver can grow back to almost full size.

bloff.q: Which country has no official capital?
bloff.fakta: Nauru is one of the world's smallest countries, with around 12,000 people.

bloff.q: How old can a Greenland shark get?
bloff.fakta: It doesn't reach maturity until it's around 150 years old.

bloff.q: Which animal has fingerprints almost identical to ours?
bloff.fakta: The prints are so similar they could in theory be mistaken for human ones at a crime scene.

bloff.q: What was the name of the first dog to orbit the Earth?
bloff.fakta: Laika was launched on Sputnik 2 in 1957.

bloff.q: What did the Norwegian Erik Rotheim invent?
bloff.fakta: Rotheim patented the idea of the aerosol can in the 1920s.

bloff.q: Which country has a flag that isn’t rectangular?
bloff.fakta: The flag is made of two triangles stacked on top of each other.

bloff.q: How many times a minute can a hummingbird’s heart beat?
bloff.fakta: The heart can beat more than 1,200 times a minute.

bloff.q: What colour is a giraffe’s tongue?
bloff.fakta: The dark colour is thought to protect the tongue from sunburn.

bloff.q: Which plant does vanilla come from?
bloff.fakta: Outside Mexico, vanilla flowers have to be pollinated by hand.

bloff.q: Who is Bluetooth named after?
bloff.fakta: The logo is Harald Bluetooth's initials written in runes.

bloff.q: Which country used paper money first?
bloff.fakta: China was using paper money more than a thousand years ago.

bloff.q: Which food practically never goes off?
bloff.fakta: Archaeologists have found honey thousands of years old in Egyptian tombs that was still edible.

bloff.q: Which land animal has the longest pregnancy?
bloff.fakta: An elephant is pregnant for about 22 months.

bloff.q: How many strings does a standard violin have?
bloff.fakta: The strings are tuned to G, D, A and E.

bloff.q: What did Walt Disney originally want to call Mickey Mouse?
bloff.fakta: It was his wife, Lillian, who suggested the name Mickey.

bloff.q: Which city has the world’s oldest underground railway?
bloff.fakta: The first line opened in 1863, with steam locomotives.
